purpose: Search the Book of the Dead for descriptions of actions and state transitions resembling the current JANUS Three Kings / Osiris return story, using AURA criteria frozen before the search.

fresh_hits.source_function: Cause Osiris to endure, give breath to the inert/weary-hearted one through Thoth, protect Osiris, calm divine conflict, and restore ordered relations.
high_value_textual_content_paraphrase: Thoth identifies himself as the agent who pacifies Horus and quiets the Two Comrades during their wrath.
He washes away blood, quiets strife and removes evil rather than solving conflict by further destruction.
The text describes Horus and Seth as mutually associated within the divine company and depicts the Two Lords working for Osiris with joyful hearts.
It describes people as friendly to one another without wrath or strife, using Isis and Nephthys as a comparison for concord.
In the same spell Thoth is described as a planner who removes evil and brings good to pass, proclaims the morrow and looks into the future while guiding cosmic domains.
Osiris is told to raise himself and endure as a living one; bodily and vital stability are restored around him.
fresh_hits.critical_role_mismatch: The ancient text assigns the planner/peace-maker/future-discerner role to THOTH, not SET. The modern Mirror-of-Set arc therefore parallels the function but cannot be claimed as an ancient doctrine about Set.
fresh_hits.why_this_is_stronger_than_symbolic_match: The match is functional: restoration of Osiris, pacification of Horus/Set, removal of wrath/strife, cooperative service and planning occur in the same spell cluster.

fresh_hits.source_function: Hymnic praise of Osiris with Thoth as truth-speaking law/order agent and reviver of Osiris.
high_value_textual_content_paraphrase: Thoth is characterized as a truth-oriented law figure whose words bring order to the two banks.
He vindicates the loser and protects the needy rather than defining right by raw force.
He gives breath to Unnofer/Osiris and revives the weary-hearted one.
A scholarly cross-check of the spell reports that Thoth removes rage, tumult and anger from the hearts of the rival gods for Osiris.
fresh_hits.critical_role_mismatch: Again, the ancient mediator is Thoth. The structural lesson can inspire the modern Set arc, but identity of roles must not be collapsed.

fresh_hits.source_function: Field-of-Offerings spell containing explicit pacification of the Two Fighters and removal of strife.
high_value_textual_content_paraphrase: Horus and Seth appear as the Two Fighters and are explicitly pacified for those among the living.
The same passage associates the resolution with creating good, bringing an offering and doing away with strife among younger generations.
fresh_hits.translation_note: Older Budge/Nebseni renderings include imagery connecting Seth with paths of the Two Eyes/Sun and Moon; the modern Allen translation instead renders this portion differently. SUN_MOON is therefore translation-sensitive and not used as a core match.

fresh_hits.source_function: Transformation spell using internal union of the Two Fighters, raising the fallen and remembrance imagery.
high_value_textual_content_paraphrase: The speaker describes joining the Two Fighters within the body through effective speech/magic.
The same sequence speaks of raising one who has fallen and remembering him.
fresh_hits.boundary: This is an internal/transformation image, not a literal description of the modern Three Kings family scene.

fresh_hits.source_function: A sacred path is associated with Thoth pacifying the Two Fighters.
Horus identifies as the one who saves and brings back his father.
fresh_hits.boundary: This supports a family-restoration motif but is not RETURN_TO_SOURCE of the lost phallus specifically.

fresh_hits.source_function: Osiris body integrity and Horus as rescuer of his father.
Going from yesterday and returning today in relation to one's limbs.
fresh_hits.boundary: Too generic to carry the Osiris-return story on its own.

previously_known_confirmatory_nodes.relevance: Body-part deity mapping including the phallus as Osirian identity in the registry's prior analysis.
Gold djed / raising and stabilization of Osiris.

strongest_new_chain.interpretation: This is the closest post-AURA source-grounded textual cluster yet found to the modern story's family-restoration and peace arc.
strongest_new_chain.note: The sequence above is a modern JANUS comparison graph assembled across different spells; the ancient Book of the Dead does not present these spells as one continuous narrative in this order.

mirror_of_set_comparison.modern_story_function: SET learns to order chaotic possibility, reduce destructive conflict, preserve alternatives and build a better future.
mirror_of_set_comparison.ancient_textual_parallel: BD182 attributes planning, peace-making, calming wrath, doing good and looking toward the morrow/future to THOTH.
mirror_of_set_comparison.safe_interpretation: The modern Set arc can be read as giving Set a constructive discipline that ancient Book-of-the-Dead material strongly associates with Thoth. This is creative recombination, not recovery of a hidden ancient Set doctrine.

kem_comparison.modern_story_function: A good boy helps without seeking ownership or kingship and becomes an example rather than a ruler.
kem_comparison.nearby_ethic: BD182/183 praise truth, help for the needy, calming violence and bringing good to pass, but they do not describe Kem's exact non-possession choice.

negative_controls: Many Egyptian texts still portray Horus/Set conflict, defeat or coercive resolution; peace passages must not erase those contrary traditions.
The Book of the Dead is a repertoire whose spell ordering varies by manuscript; JANUS cross-spell chains are analytical graphs, not reconstructed ancient chapter order.
Thoth is the explicit ancient mediator/planner in the strongest fresh hit, preventing a false claim that Set already held the modern Mirror-of-Set role in the source.
